brief_rationale: The doctor recognized the diabetic-foot postoperative wound with bone-cement detachment as needing urgent in-person/ED evaluation, acted on odor/drainage and hyperglycemia, and gave safe interim medication boundaries rather than unsupported insulin dose escalation. The caregiver demonstrably executed the pathway, brought records/medications, and the patient reached the original hospital ED with wound review, labs, culture, antibiotics, and inpatient/observational ownership. High-order credit is supported for practical navigation of the access/documentation gap, dynamic reprioritization as wound and glucose information evolved, and bounded open handoff to the hospital team. No responsibility-chain error or important non-chain defect is evident, so the trajectory reaches Perfect.
